The 7th schedule of the Constitution deals with the division of powers between centre and state. By 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016, added Article 246A, Notwithstanding anything contained in Article 246 and 254, Parliament, and subject to clause (2), the legislature of every state, have power to make laws with respect to goods and services tax imposed by the Union or by such state. *Article 249 deals with the Power of Parliament to legislate with respect to a matter in the state list in the national interest. *If the Rajya Sabha declares that it is necessary in the national interest that Parliament should make laws on a matter in the state list, then the Parliament becomes competent to make laws on that matter. *Such a resolution must be supported by 2/3rd of the members present and voting. * Article 250 (1) empowers the Parliament to legislative with respect to a matter in the state list if a proclamation of emergency is in Progress, Article 251 States that if there is in consistency between laws made by Parliament under Art. 249 & Art 250 and laws made by the legislature of States, then the laws made by the Parliament shall prevail. *Article 252 deals with the power of Parliament to legislate for two or more States by consent and adoption of such legislation by any other state. *Article 253 deals with legislations giving eﬀ ect to international agreements. The Parliament can make laws on any matter in the state list for implementing the international treaties, agreements and conventions. This provision enables the Central Government to fulﬁ l its international obligations and commitments. Administrative Relations : *Articles 256 to 263 in Part XI of the Constitution deals with the administrative relations between centre and States. *Article 256 deals with the obligations of States and the Union. *The executive power of centre intends to giving such directions to the States as are necessary for the purpose. *Article 257 deals with the control of the Union over States in certain cases. *Article 258 deals with the power of the Union to confer powers, etc, on States in certain cases. *Accordingly the President may, with the consent of the state government, entrust to that government any of the executive functions of the Centre. *Article 262 (1) deals with Adjudication of disputes relating to water of inter-state rivers or valleys. *Article 263 allows the President to establish an Inter-state Council to investigate and discuss subjects of common interest between the centre and the States. Such a council was setup in 1990. Financial Relations : *Article 264 to 293 in part XII of the Constitution deals with centre-state ﬁ nancial relations. *Article 265 of the Indian Constitution deals with levy of tax. The article States that “No tax shall be levied or collected except by the authority of law.” *Article 266 (1) of the Constitution of India deals with the establishment of a Consolidate Fund of India, where all revenues received by union government as well as all loans and all money received by the Union Government in repayment of loans shall form the part of the fund. The Contingency Fund of India is established under Article 267 (1) of the Constitution. By The Constitution (One Hundred and ﬁ rst Amendment) Act, 2016, Article 279 A was added for Goods and Services Tax Council. *According to Article 267 (2) the legislature of the state may by law establish a Contingency Fund in the nature of an imprest to be entitled the Contingency Fund of the state. *Article 275 deals with the Grants allocated by the Union to certain States. *A new Article 269A has been inserted into the Constitution by 'The Constitution (one hundred and ﬁ rst Amendment) Act, 2016. This Article deals with levy and collection of goods and services tax in course of inter-state trade or commerce. *According to Article 280 (1) of the Constitution of India, a Finance Commission should be set up as a quasi judicial body. *It is constituted by the President after 2 years of enactment and enforcement of the Constitution of India and thereon every 5th year or at such earlier time as he considers necessary. *According to Article 281 the President lays down the report of the Finance Commission before both the houses of the Parliament along with an explanatory memorandum as to the actions taken on its recommendations. *In 1983 the Central Government appointed a three member Commission on centre-state Relations under the Chairmanship of R.S. Sarkaria a retired Judge of the Supreme Court. Hence the name Sarkaria Commission was given. B. Shivraman and S.R. Sen were the other two members of this Commission. The ﬁ nal Report was submitted in January, 1988. *Rajamannar Committee and Punchhi Commission are also associated with Centre-State relations. 1. The Centre-State relations in India are inﬂ uenced by: 1. Provisions of the Constitution 2. The Planning process

optionsEn: Five Zonal Councils have set up under the State Reorganisation Act, 1956
Chandigarh although not a state, is included in Zonal Council
optionsHi: राज्य पुनर्गठन अधिनियम, 1956 के तहत पांच क्षेत्रीय परिषदें स्थापित की गई हैं
